title: JUST IN: Two National Guardsmen In CRITICAL Condition After White House Shooting
text:
The recent shooting incident in Washington, D.C., which left two National Guardsmen critically injured, has sent shockwaves throughout the nation. This targeted attack occurred near the White House, underscoring the gravity of security risks in a city that is both the heart of American power and a symbol of national resilience. FBI Director Kash Patel characterized the guardsmen as “heroes,” highlighting their dedication even amid adversity and urging Americans to offer prayers for their recovery.
The incident unfolded around 2:15 p.m. on November 26, 2024, near Farragut Square. Witnesses described the scene as chaotic, with rapid gunfire echoing through the streets. The two guardsmen, members of the West Virginia National Guard, were on foot patrol as part of a security initiative aimed at countering rising crime in the capital. In response, the Trump administration had deployed approximately 2,000 troops in August 2024. In the aftermath of the shooting, President Trump ordered an additional 500 guardsmen to bolster security efforts, emphasizing the urgency of the situation.
The suspect, identified as Rahmanullah Lakanwal, reportedly ambushed the guardsmen as they patrolled the area. Metropolitan Police Assistant Chief Jeff Carroll labeled the assault an “ambush,” reflecting the premeditated nature of the attack. This designation raises critical questions about security protocols and the vulnerabilities faced by those sworn to protect citizens. Carroll recounted how, after the initial shots, the guardsmen responded heroically, managing to subdue Lakanwal despite being shot themselves.
Eyewitness accounts offer a glimpse into the panic that ensued as bystanders fled in fear. One witness, Stacy Walters, recalled hearing distinct gunfire before seeing people run. Another, Mike Ryan, witnessed the valor of the guardsmen as they attempted to resuscitate their injured comrades. Such descriptions illustrate not only the chaos of that moment but also the courage displayed by those who serve.
The investigation, now overseen by the FBI, has raised national security concerns due to Lakanwal’s immigration history. Entering the U.S. under Operation Allies Welcome in 2021, he was granted asylum in April 2025 without a documented criminal record prior to this incident. This fact has reignited debates surrounding immigration policies, particularly those enacted during the Biden administration. Critics argue that security vetting processes need significant improvement to prevent individuals with potential ties to extremism from entering the country.
President Trump’s immediate response highlighted the seriousness of the crime. He condemned the shooting as an “act of evil, an act of hatred, and an act of terror,” vowing that Lakanwal would face severe consequences. His remarks reflect a broader concern regarding public safety amidst the backdrop of immigration reform. As scrutiny increases, officials are calling for a formal congressional review of the policies that allowed for the expedited acceptance of Afghan refugees like Lakanwal.
The shooting not only raises pressing questions about public safety but also reveals deeper anxieties regarding national security and immigration. With discussions of capping refugee admissions to a mere 7,500 for fiscal year 2026 and a pause on further processing for Afghan nationals, policymakers are now faced with reconciling humanitarian obligations against potential risks. This tension is palpable, as Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth referred to the incident as a “cowardly, dastardly act,” reiterating the necessity for stringent security measures.
There is acknowledgment from military leadership as well. Maj. Gen. Tim Seward praised the swift actions of the other guardsmen in neutralizing the shooter, emphasizing their bravery as pivotal in preventing further tragedy. Such reflections reinforce the commitment of service members who place their lives on the line to protect their fellow Americans.
As two critically injured guardsmen receive medical attention, their families remain at the forefront of concern. The Pentagon has pledged to keep the public updated on their condition, further emphasizing the human toll of this violence. FBI Director Patel’s assurance of a comprehensive investigation underscores the need for accountability and transparency in the wake of the attack.
The choice of weapon in this incident—a semiautomatic handgun—adds another layer to the ongoing discourse about gun violence and national security. Investigators are now examining Lakanwal’s electronic devices and travel history for potential connections to extremist groups. This scrutiny reflects the administration’s resolve to confront threats head-on while addressing the critical question of how an asylum recipient could carry out such an act.
This tragic shooting serves as both a painful reminder and a catalyst for urgent discussions about safety and immigration. As the nation reflects on this event, it becomes clear that questions surrounding national security will remain a pressing issue in the political discourse to come. President Trump has indicated that reviews of past admissions will take place, suggesting that future policies will be informed by the lessons learned from this incident. Flags across West Virginia and at National Guard installations are at half-staff, symbolizing a collective mourning and respect for those who serve with honor.
